systemPrompt: You are an academic task planning assistant. Your job is to decompose a given academic writing deliverable into a set of specific, actionable microtasks that a student can execute one at a time. Each microtask should be small enough to complete in a single focused session and clearly worded. For each microtask, identify which other microtasks, if any, must be completed first, referencing them by ID; microtasks with no prerequisites may be worked on immediately, and independent sub-goals should be expressed as separate, non-blocking strands rather than forced into a single chain. Do not give advice, explanations, or motivational language. Output only a single JSON object, with no text before or after it, in exactly this format: {"microtasks": [{"id": <integer>, "description": "<microtask>", "prerequisites": [<ids>]}]}. Use an empty array for microtasks with no prerequisites.
userPrompt: I need to write the related literature section of our research paper on the effects of social media use on teenagers. I do not know where to start. Create microtasks that would help me write this section of the paper.

<thought>Write the "Related Literature" section of a research paper on "the effects of social media use on teenagers."
Decompose into actionable microtasks.
JSON object with `id`, `description`, and `prerequisites`.

    *   Phase 1: Preparation & Search
        *   Define scope/keywords.
        *   Search databases.
        *   Filter/Select papers.
    *   Phase 2: Reading & Synthesis
        *   Read selected papers.
        *   Extract key findings/theories.
        *   Identify themes/gaps.
    *   Phase 3: Outlining
        *   Create a thematic structure.
        *   Map literature to themes.
    *   Phase 4: Drafting
        *   Write introduction to the section.
        *   Write theme 1.
        *   Write theme 2.
        *   Write theme 3.
        *   Write summary/gap identification.
    *   Phase 5: Refinement
        *   Check citations.
        *   Edit for flow.

    *   *Task 1:* Define specific research questions/sub-topics (e.g., mental health, sleep, social comparison).
    *   *Task 2:* Identify keywords and search terms.
    *   *Task 3:* Search academic databases (Google Scholar, PubMed, etc.).
    *   *Task 4:* Screen search results for relevance and quality.
    *   *Task 5:* Read selected papers and take notes on methodology and findings.
    *   *Task 6:* Create a synthesis matrix (table of authors, themes, findings).
    *   *Task 7:* Identify recurring themes and research gaps.
    *   *Task 8:* Create a thematic outline for the literature review.
    *   *Task 9:* Write the introductory paragraph of the literature review.
    *   *Task 10:* Draft the subsection for Theme A.
    *   *Task 11:* Draft the subsection for Theme B.
    *   *Task 12:* Draft the subsection for Theme C.
    *   *Task 13:* Write the summary paragraph connecting literature to the current study's gap.
    *   *Task 14:* Verify all in-text citations against the reference list.
    *   *Task 15:* Review and edit for transitions and academic tone.

    *   1 (Define questions) -> 2 (Keywords) -> 3 (Search) -> 4 (Screen) -> 5 (Read/Notes) -> 6 (Matrix) -> 7 (Themes/Gaps) -> 8 (Outline).
    *   8 (Outline) -> 9 (Intro), 10 (Theme A), 11 (Theme B), 12 (Theme C), 13 (Summary).
    *   9, 10, 11, 12, 13 -> 14 (Citations) -> 15 (Edit).

    *   *Self-Correction during drafting:* Task 1 and 2 can be separate. Task 5 and 6 are closely linked. Task 10, 11, 12 are parallel.

    *   1: Define specific research sub-topics (e.g., mental health, body image, sleep). [Prereq: []]
    *   2: Generate a list of search keywords and Boolean operators. [Prereq: [1]]
    *   3: Conduct database searches using keywords. [Prereq: [2]]
    *   4: Screen search results based on title and abstract for relevance. [Prereq: [3]]
    *   5: Read full texts of selected papers and extract key findings/methodologies. [Prereq: [4]]

    *   7: Identify major themes and research gaps from the synthesis matrix. [Prereq: [6]]
    *   8: Create a thematic outline for the literature review section. [Prereq: [7]]
    *   9: Write the introductory paragraph defining the scope of the review. [Prereq: [8]]
    *   10: Draft the subsection for the first identified theme. [Prereq: [8]]
    *   11: Draft the subsection for the second identified theme. [Prereq: [8]]
    *   12: Draft the subsection for the third identified theme. [Prereq: [8]]
    *   13: Write the concluding paragraph summarizing the literature and highlighting the research gap. [Prereq: [8]]
    *   14: Cross-check all in-text citations with the bibliography. [Prereq: [9, 10, 11, 12, 13]]
    *   15: Edit the section for logical flow and academic tone. [Prereq: [14]]
